newsitem.title: USA: Crude oil off on ample stocks, Iraqi sales fears.
newsitem.headline: Crude oil off on ample stocks, Iraqi sales fears.

text.p: Crude oil prices fell Thursday due partly to a weekly report that showed ample domestic supplies and on concerns that Iraq would increase sales.
Gold prices rose sharply. Coffee futures also posted strong gains amid tight supplies.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, crude oil for March delivery fell 81 cents to $21.98 a barrel, just above the day's low of $21.90.
"The API numbers were pretty bearish, and the Iraq news did not help," said a New York crude dealer.
The United Nations sanctions committee on Iraq approved deeper discounts for Iraqi crude sales to the United States, diplomatic sources said Thursday.
Oil traders said the increased discount for Iraqi oil for late February and early March period might encourage even more Iraqi crude to head to the United States.
Under a deal approved last December, the United Nations eased sanctions against Iraq to allow it to sell $2 billion worth of oil for six months in exchange for humanitarian aid.
In adddition, the American Petroleum Institute (API) reported Wednesday that domestic crude oil stocks rose 3.1 million barrels for the week ended Feb. 14.
The data also showed crude oil stocks were higher than at this time last year, the first time in 15 months that stocks have increased compared with a year earlier.
Heating oil and gasoline also fell, with March heating oil off 1.55 cents to 58.04 cents, and March gasoline down 1.90 cents to 62.78 cents.
Coffee futures on New York's Coffee, Sugar, Cocoa Exchange ended higher after a rollercoaster ride as profit-taking knocked prices off earlier contract highs.
"It bounced back and forth like the stock market does," said Smith Barney analyst Walt Spilka. "I would be somewhat wary but the underlying fundamentals have not changed and those are bullish."
"Stocks of arabica coffees remain tight and do not show much sign that they will increase significantly," he added.
March coffee ended up 3.15 cents at 178.45 cents a pound, well below an earlier contract high of 183.50 cents.

Prices have climbed about 70 percent in two months and Folgers Coffee Co. said Thursday it had tripled its increase on the list price on its standard 13-ounce can of coffee to 45 cents, rather than the 15-cent increase announced Feb. 10.
The increase, which takes effect on March 3, brings the price of a standard can to $2.71, the company said.

Gold prices on New York's Commodity Exchange (COMEX) closed sharply higher with sentiment helped by news that the South African Reserve Bank governor, Chris Stals, said he thought the Belgian and Dutch central bank gold sales last year would not be followed by other central bank gold sales.
Gold prices saw three-year lows last week, fuelled partly by fears of further European central bank gold sales.
Comex April gold ended up $5 an ounce at $352.60, after climbing to $354.00, its highest level since Jan. 29.
